input_oneliner: 77M HTN, AF, anticoag held for GI bleed, continuous room-spinning since 2 AM with vomiting, cannot walk to bathroom, BP 168/94

optional_context.comorbidity: hypertension, atrial fibrillation with anticoagulation held

reference_targets_freetext.item: HINTS exam (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Normal head impulse, direction-changing nystagmus, or skew indicates central cause in acute vestibular syndrome

reference_targets_freetext.item: Assess gait and truncal ataxia: can the patient sit unsupported and stand or walk unassisted
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Inability to stand or walk unaided strongly favors a central lesion

reference_targets_freetext.item: Confirm timing and triggers: continuous vs episodic, and whether head movement provokes the vertigo or merely worsens it
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Determines that HINTS (not Dix-Hallpike) is the right test

reference_targets_freetext.item: Focused cranial nerve and cerebellar exam: dysarthria, diplopia, dysphagia, limb dysmetria, facial numbness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Additional posterior circulation signs; absence does not exclude stroke

reference_targets_freetext.item: Bedside hearing check (finger rub) for new unilateral hearing loss (HINTS-plus)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: New hearing loss with vertigo favors AICA territory stroke over neuritis

off_bedside_acceptable: MRI brain with diffusion-weighted imaging (CT is insensitive for posterior fossa)
should_not_recommend: Dix-Hallpike or Epley maneuver in continuous spontaneous vertigo
Meclizine and reassess in the morning without a neurologic examination
Rely on a normal non-contrast head CT to exclude posterior circulation stroke

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: timing/trigger: continuous spontaneous vertigo -> brief episodes triggered by rolling over, well between
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 77M HTN, AF, anticoag held for GI bleed, spinning for seconds each time he rolls over since 2 AM, nauseated, walks fine, BP 168/94
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Dix-Hallpike maneuver becomes must_have and bppv rises to top of differential; HINTS exam drops (not interpretable without continuous vertigo and spontaneous nystagmus); gait assessment remains included.
